newsitem.title: UK: Frontline says encouraged by bond market.
newsitem.headline: Frontline says encouraged by bond market.

text.p: A buoyant market for tanker company bond issues has encouraged Frontline Ltd to consider its own issue to finance four VLCCs, the tanker company said on Friday.
Frontline director Tor Olav Troim told Reuters: "We have seen what has been going on in the bond market over the past two months, and believe it may be a good way to finance these new ships."
He cited the recent bond issues launched by Global Ocean Carriers Ltd, Golden Ocean Group Ltd and Equimar Shipholdings Ltd, a subsidiary of B&H Ocean Carriers Ltd.
"We have seen what those tanker firms have done," said Troim. "If investors continue to look for a 10 percent annual return, then we have to use the bond market."
He reaffirmed Frontline's intention to seek a secondary listing in the US later this year. The firm is already listed in Oslo.
But Troim refused to comment on the progress of negotiations for the possible acquisition of London & Overseas Freighters Plc.
"You will have to get an answer out of LOFs on that one," he said.

The Bermuda-based tanker owner said earlier it was looking at a bond issue to finance the construction of four VLCCs, set to be built at South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries. -Reuters Shipping News +44 171 542 4087/4012 Fax 542 5017
